facts.fact: Starting retirement contributions earlier, even at a smaller amount, generally requires less total money invested to reach the same eventual balance than starting later, due to compounding over a longer time horizon.
facts.caveat: Illustrative principle; actual outcomes depend on returns, contribution consistency, and market conditions, which are never guaranteed.

facts.fact: Common first-job financial priorities cited by financial educators include building a small emergency fund, capturing any employer retirement match, and starting a credit history responsibly.
facts.caveat: General guidance; individual priorities depend on debt load, income, and circumstances.

facts.fact: Buying a home involves upfront costs beyond the purchase price (closing costs, inspection, moving, maintenance reserve) that are commonly underestimated by first-time buyers.
facts.caveat: Exact costs vary enormously by location and situation; no single percentage applies everywhere.

facts.fact: Major life transitions (marriage, having children, a first home) are commonly recommended checkpoints for revisiting beneficiaries, insurance coverage, and budgets.
facts.caveat: General financial-planning guidance, not individualized advice.

facts.fact: The concept of a 'financial independence number' (a savings target enabling a sustainable withdrawal rate to cover living expenses) is commonly estimated using a multiple of annual expenses in independence/FIRE community discussions.
facts.caveat: Based on general withdrawal-rate discussions; not a guarantee, and sustainable withdrawal rates are debated among researchers.
